nav (sre): heads-up: dry-run for AZ routing failover tomorrow 02:00 UTC. Purpose: validate route failover scripts and measure session reconnects. Expect brief reconnects (~5-12s) for tunnel endpoints. No customer action.

ivy (oncall): will pages fire? what's the alert sensitivity for the dry-run?

nav (sre): pages only if error-rate > 0.7% OR BGP-down > 45s. We'll mute noisy connection-reset alerts during the window; specific page rules unchanged.

sam (infra): plan: 1) shift traffic from primary-router to standby 2) validate BGP convergence 3) run health probes and synthetic at 2m/10m/30m after shift. Script snippet:
```
# failover helper
./ops/failover --router primary-az1 --target standby-az1 --monitor 60s
```

tara (prod-eng): can we pin low-latency model-serving routes to avoid evicting warmed kv caches? we saw cold-cache P99 spikes last time.

nav (sre): good catch. We'll keep kv-cache pinning for VIP routes for the canary traffic. Ops-bot will run pre-warm job.

infra-bot: Preflight: bgp-peers=OK, kv-cache=90%, router-health=green. Dry-run schedule created.

ivy (oncall): I'll be on-call. If we see P99 > 200ms for 10m we'll rollback. Also will monitor Dedicated pool allocation logs.

nav (sre): rollback plan: reattach original routes, revert route-map, and re-run sync job. If BGP flaps > 60s open incident and escalate.

pagerduty: Pager escalation set to ivy -> nav -> infra.

tara (prod-eng): I'll run a quick synthetic through edge and post results here after the dry-run.

nav (sre): thanks. action items: sam update runbook with script path, infra-bot attach final checklist, tara run synthetics, ivy hold pages. Meeting invite sent.

sam (infra): runbook updated: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/az-failover-dryrun-2026

nav (sre): closing thread. Will post post-run metrics in #eng-sre after tests complete. :white_check_mark:
